subject: Hosted API pricing: monthly run‑rate deep dive & spike profile
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma@novalabs.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-08-14T13:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API pricing: monthly run‑rate deep dive & spike profile

Thanks again for taking the time today, Emma — good conversation. Quick recap and two asks so we can model unit economics and get you a tight hosted quote: 

Call highlights
- Primary integration: user-facing NLU + summarization (post‑chat) across mobile + web.
- Expected steady-state: mostly short prompts (avg tokens/request ~ 350).
- Spike behavior: 1–2 weekly marketing pushes that could triple QPS for ~30–90 minutes.

Asks / data we need to finalize pricing (bold = highest impact)
1) Confirm expected monthly token volume range (low/likely/high) — we used your ballpark: 15M / 45M / 120M tokens.
2) Confirm peak TPS during campaign spikes (99th percentile) — you mentioned ~400 TPS at peak; is 350–450 accurate?
3) Target unit cost target ($ per 1M tokens) or monthly budget band we should aim for — you said ~USD 750–1,200 / 1M as an internal target? Confirm.
4) Any data residency / VPC requirements (affects Private vs Hosted).

I attached a quick template (nova_usage_sheet.xlsx) — could you fill the colored cells or reply with the exact ranges? Once we have those we will:
- Run cost scenarios (quantization + batching assumptions) and return 3 options: conservative (no quant), balanced (mixed), aggressive (8‑bit/quant) with expected $/1M, 99th TPS SLO, and recommended routing policy for spikes.

Next steps
- You: confirm items 1–3 and upload the usage template by EOD Wed if possible.
- Us: 48-hour turn for a hosted pricing recommendation and sample SLA language.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555‑0147

Attachments: nova_usage_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet — fill the blue cells); redwood_rate_card_v2.pdf (reference rates)

From: Emma Chen <emma@novalabs.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-08-14T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: monthly run‑rate deep dive & spike profile

Thanks, Olga — great call. Quick answers inline: 

1) Monthly tokens (low/typical/high): 12M / 40M / 110M (these are monthly active prompt tokens only; includes summarization).
2) Peak TPS: our recent campaigns pushed to ~380 TPS for ~45 minutes. We design to handle 500 TPS for brief spikes but historically haven’t exceeded ~400.
3) Budget target: we are trying to keep marginal cost near USD 900 / 1M tokens; procurement will push, but product prefers not to be above 1,200.
4) No VPC required for this initial rollout — Hosted is fine, but we need SOC2 evidence for procurement (they may ask).

I uploaded a filled version of the template to the Drive link — file name: Nova_NLU_usage_filled_Aug14.xlsx. Let me know if the numbers need further breakdown by endpoint.

—Emma
CTO (acting) | Nova Labs
emma@novalabs.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-08-15T09:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing: monthly run‑rate deep dive & spike profile

Forwarding Emma's filled template and the numbers she confirmed. Key modeling inputs below — please run the 3 scenario sketches and return an estimate we can share with Nova: 
- Monthly tokens: 12M / 40M / 110M (steady-state prompts only). Avg tokens/request = 350.
- Peak: 380 TPS observed, tolerance to design for short bursts to 500 TPS.
- Budget target: ~USD 900 / 1M preferred, procurement ceiling 1,200 / 1M.
- No VPC for now; procurement will request SOC2 evidence.

Please include: 
- Unit $/1M for each scenario (hosted).
- Expected 99th latency at peak (p50/p95/p99).
- Ops notes on recommended burst policy (e.g., reserved capacity + burst to shared).
- Any assumptions about batching, kv cache hit rate (I assume 15% prefix reuse), and quantization.

Attach the pricing sketches to return to Emma within 48 hours.

Olga

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-08-15T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API pricing: monthly run‑rate deep dive & spike profile

Copy — we'll model this. Initial assumptions (to validate):
- Conservative: no quantization, baseline batching = 8 reqs/token batch, unit = USD 1,350 / 1M for 12M band, with 99th at peak ~420 TPS -> 220 ms.
- Balanced: mixed quantization, batching heuristics + cache -> ~USD 980 / 1M for 40M band, 99th at peak ~380 TPS -> 280 ms.
- Aggressive: aggressive 8‑bit quant + bigger batching, requires small model changes -> ~USD 720 / 1M at 110M band, 99th at peak ~360 TPS -> 340 ms (note higher variability).

Questions: does Nova have a hard SLA requirement on 99th latency? If they require <250 ms at 99th under 400 TPS we should recommend Dedicated instead of Hosted.

I'll produce the spreadsheet with line‑item math and the tradeoffs; will include a recommended routing policy: reserved capacity supporting base 450 TPS + dynamic burst to hosted pool for marketing spikes. Returning estimate by EOD Fri.

—Vanessa
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: Emma Chen <emma@novalabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-08-16T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: monthly run‑rate deep dive & spike profile

Thanks — that breakdown looks helpful. A few clarifications from procurement before we lock: 
- Procurement asks for SOC2 report PDF and standard hosted terms (we can start with your standard SLA).
- If Hosted can’t guarantee <250 ms p99 at sustained 400 TPS, we’ll evaluate a small Dedicated reserve for peak windows.
- Our internal target remains ~USD 900 / 1M; if you can present a balanced option near that number with clear assumptions, procurement will be comfortable moving to a short PO.

I'll wait for the spreadsheet and the formal quote. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Emma
Procurement cc: procurement@novalabs.com
